seo-intelligence.purpose: Perplexity Search API + SERP + GSC + HubSpot + Places (24 tools). RUNG 1 of the research skill's tool ladder — ~$0.005/query flat, never the $5-40 chat models
seo-intelligence.whenToLoad: research/search tasks FIRST (prefer over web_search); also GSC, SERP, Places and HubSpot tasks. NOTE: requires a one-time `npm install` in mcp-servers/seo-intelligence per checkout, or the entry fails to spawn

tortoise._comment: HOSTED Tortoise MCP over HTTP. This replaced the legacy stdio entry (${TORTOISE_HOME}/.venv/bin/python3 -m tortoise.mcp_server + a local TORTOISE_DB_URI=docker://...:16379) that needed a tortoise checkout, a venv AND a local FalkorDB — none of which exists on a cmux cloud cell, which is why pi-bootstrap/cell-install.sh refused to install this file on cells at all and every fleet lane on a cell ran with ZERO MCP servers, writing GRAPH-UNREACHABLE into its report. The DB target is resolved SERVER-SIDE (FALKORDB_CLOUD_URI), so a client needs only the endpoint and the key. Auth is env-indirect: ${TORTOISE_API_KEY} is canonical (#5153/#5343) and TORTOISE_MCP_API_KEY is the fleet alias, which must be aliased because a plain ${VAR} expands to the EMPTY STRING when unset and the server then answers 401 instead of failing loudly. lazy=true is deliberate: the hosted server's cold handshake routinely exceeds pi's default MCP connect budget, and this entry now lands on memory-constrained cells where a core server would block every session start. Self-host users point url at their own daemon instead (http://localhost:8000/mcp — docs/quickstart-selfhosted.md).
tortoise.purpose: Memory graph (Tortoise, hosted) — read before you derive, write what you learn
tortoise.whenToLoad: any lane: graph read before research, write-back after (`mcp_load tortoise`)
tortoise.cost: one HTTP session; lazy, so nothing is paid while it sleeps
